new_statements.rule_in_words: The grammar states that Tarao has no suprasegmental phonemes at all (tone and juncture are the examples named), i.e. no contrastive prosodic feature at word level; stress is not mentioned anywhere in the book, so no placement rule is given and no predictable (non-phonemic) stress is described either.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the book's scanned text contains no occurrence of 'stress', 'stressed', 'accent', 'pitch', 'prominence', 'intonation', 'tonal' or 'non-tonal'.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the phoneme inventory of the language (word-level phonology, citation forms); nothing on phrase-level prosody. Quote is verbatim scanned retrieved as search-hit snippets from the Internet Archive full-text index of the lending-restricted scan (three overlapping windows joined; 'supra- segmental' is a line-break hyphen in the scanned); the page itself was not viewed.
new_statements.identity_note: The language described by Singh 2002 is the Tarao of Tarao Khullen (Tarao Laimanai), Leishok Ching and Khuringmul villages, Chandel district, Manipur = tara1313 [tro] (Northwestern/Old Kuki-Chin); no dialect split is involved. Caution on identity in the catalogue records: the Library of Congress subject heading on Singh 2002 ('Digaro language--Grammar', copied into the archive.org item) and Glottolog reference 679419 (NEFA 1963, A Dictionary of the Taraon Language, tagged [diga1241];[tara1313]) both confuse Tarao with Taraon = Digaro-Mishmi (diga1241, Arunachal Pradesh); the 1963 dictionary does not concern this language.
